events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Muskegon or Grand Haven for boat salmon this week.** My rating for both is **3 (good)**, based on the newest reports.
- **Muskegon (3):** Troll 120 to 200 ft of water with fish 35 to 90 ft down. Green and blue spoons and white flies worked best.
- **Grand Haven (3):** Troll 130 to 240 ft of water with fish 30 to 120 ft down. This is the same report as Muskegon, with less lure detail.
- **St. Joseph (3, mostly coho):** Spoons from 40 ft out to well past 120 ft. Expect mostly coho, with few Chinook.
- **South Haven (2, average):** Spoons, with fish spread from 30 ft down to deeper water. It was the weakest of the four in the latest report.
- **Caveat:** Ratings are estimates from reports that are 6 days old. Live wind and cold-layer data were unavailable, so check the forecast before launching.

## Why

- **Muskegon and Grand Haven are my top picks:** The May 18 reports rated boat fishing good (3) at both, with fish holding 30 to 120 ft down.
- **St. Joseph is close behind:** Its May 18 boat report was good (3), but the catch was mostly coho, and Chinook were only a few.
- **South Haven is rated lower:** Its May 18 boat report was only fair (2), and the May 4 report was slow (1).
- **My rating for this week is an inference:** I'd expect the bite to hold near these levels, since the surface water is in the 52 to 53 F range that salmon prefer, but no report covers this week yet.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (the newest is May 18, six days before today)
- Muskegon, 2022-05-18, boat: "Boats were doing well catching salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water." Green and blue spoons and white flies worked; a few fish came on meat rigs. Quality 3.
- Grand Haven, 2022-05-18, boat: "The salmon action was good 30 to 120 feet down in 130 to 240 feet of water." Quality 3. The pier was slow, with a few coho on alewives or orange spoons.
- St. Joseph, 2022-05-18, boat: "Boat anglers targeting salmon had good fishing." Catches were mostly coho and steelhead on spoons, with a few Chinook. Boats fished from 40 ft out to well past 120 ft. Coho quality 3, Chinook quality 1.
- South Haven, 2022-05-18, boat: "Boat anglers targeting salmon had fair fishing." Most boats trolled spoons, and fish were spread from 30 ft down to deeper water. Quality 2.
- Earlier, on 2022-05-04: St. Joseph boats rated good (3) for coho at 30 ft; Grand Haven and South Haven were slow (1), with South Haven's fish scattered at 35 to 45 ft.

**Past seasons:** A search of earlier years with similar surface water (about 52 F) returned only the same May 18 reports, so I have no independent history to add.

**Conditions now** (the tool returned a backtest summary for the week before May 24, not live data)
- Surface water (measured, buoy 45168 for St. Joseph and South Haven, buoy 45029 for Grand Haven and Muskegon): about 52 to 53 F, down 3 to 4 F over the week.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52 to 58 F, which the surface water is in now.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant): a sharp drop in buoy surface temperature can signal upwelling. A 3 to 4 F drop is modest, so I'd expect only a mild effect, but I can't confirm it from these data.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from May 18, six days old. The bite can change quickly, so check the latest DNR bulletin before you go.
- Live wind and modeled cold-layer depth were unavailable, so I couldn't check the forecast or the depth of the cold water. Wind matters for a small boat on Lake Michigan.
- The ratings are my estimates from one week of reports per port. Grand Haven and Muskegon rely on the same bulletin, and St. Joseph's good rating is mostly for coho.

## Sources

- DNR bulletin, May 18, 2022 (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- DNR bulletin, May 4, 2022 (Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
